item.title: Dell XPS 16 review: Two steps forward, one step back
item.description: The 2026 XPS 16 makes massive gains in terms of efficiency and design. Nonetheless, some key sacrifices were made that buyers should be aware of.

item.title: Orbital Pathfinder mouse review: Infinite customization, with a great mouse to boot
item.description: A hands-on review of the Orbitalworks Pathfinder gaming mouse. Where performance meets ergonomics.

item.title: Intel Core Ultra 200S Plus review: More cores and more power for gamers starting at $199
item.description: In this review, we analyze the performance of the Core Ultra 7 270K Plus and the Core Ultra 5 250K Plus in everyday use as well as their gaming performance in combination with an Nvidia GeForce RTX 4090.

item.title: Better than Dreame, Roborock &amp; Co? Eureka J15 Max Ultra review
item.description: The Eureka J15 Max Ultra impresses in the test with solid cleaning, but clearly falls behind top models from Roborock and Dreame when it comes to obstacle detection and innovation.

item.title: A game to cry over: Death Stranding 2 for PC in review
item.description: We subject Death Stranding 2 to a technical and benchmark check with various laptop and desktop GPUs.

item.title: Affordable cordless vacuum with bend-and-mop function: Proscenic P20 OnePass hands-on test
item.description: Versatile. | A cordless vacuum that can also mop? That is exactly what the Proscenic P20 OnePass promises, without actually being a wet/dry vacuum. Our hands-on test shows what that means in practice.

item.title: Honor Magic8 Pro Air review: A dream come true for many smartphone fans
item.description: Ultra-light with no major compromises. | On paper, the Magic8 Pro Air is the Android phone many have been waiting for. This slim high-end phone is lightweight and compact without making major sacrifices in chipset performance or camera hardware. The Honor handset also impresses with top-tier specs.

item.title: A big seller despite many cut corners: Apple iPhone 17e smartphone review
item.description: Unfortunately fantastic. | Whether you like it or not, the iPhone 17e is likely to be a bestseller. By Apple's standards, it's inexpensive and, objectively speaking, offers decent features that make everyday tasks a breeze. However, comparisons with the other iPhone 17 models and some competitors that cost less than half as much are less flattering.

item.title: Alldocube iWork GT Ultra convertible review: Alternative to Android tablets with true PC performance
item.description: Solid performance, clear compromises. | With the iWork GT Ultra, Alldocube offers a versatile Windows convertible with Intel Core Ultra 5 125H. The stylus and keyboard cover are available as a complete package for around $920. But how does the device perform in everyday use in terms of performance, mobility, and battery life? Our test answers the most important questions.

item.title: Sunseeker V1 review: Bargain robotic lawnmower for English lawn
item.description: Extremely cheap, but with a garage. | A robotic lawnmower for under 400 euros sounds like a real bargain. In the test, however, the Sunseeker V1 quickly shows that the low-cost robotic lawnmower does not guarantee an English lawn, but rather requires it - and even dug itself in once.

item.title: Oneisall Ease S1 auto litterbox review: Looks as good as it performs
item.description: Goes above and beyond the call of duty. | The Oneisall Ease S1 takes a decisively stylistic and functional approach to tackle one, if not the worst, challenge of cat ownership. With easy setup, clever mechanics, and a system that is easy to clean, the Ease S1 makes quick work of cat box maintenance, and it does it in style.

item.title: Zendure SolarFlow 2400 Pro review: Is the XXL balcony solar system with 2,400 W & AI worth it?
item.description: BKW overkill? | A balcony solar system that works almost like a large PV system? That's exactly what the Zendure SolarFlow 2400 Pro promises - with AI, dynamic electricity tariffs and up to 16.8 kWh of storage. Is the expensive XXL storage system worth it in everyday life or is it simply too much?

item.title: Compact & affordable smart lock with Matter: Yale Linus L2 Lite review
item.description: Smart Lock instead of a key. | As compact as a premium model, but still affordable. The Linus Smart Lock L2 Lite comes in a handy format complete with Matter. Our test reveals who the bargain smart lock is suitable for and what compromises need to be made.

item.title: Samsung Galaxy Book6 Pro Laptop Review - Better than the new XPS 16
item.description: The least interesting Panther Lake CPU. | Samsung's new Galaxy Book6 Pro gets Intel's Panther Lake processors, Wi-Fi 7 as well as a new OLED touchscreen, which is finally brighter than before. Prices are very high, however, and the Galaxy Book6 Pro faces excellent rivals, so is it enough to beat the XPS 16 or Zenbook S16?

item.title: Old but affordable in times of RAM crisis: Lenovo ThinkPad T14 Gen 6 AMD laptop review
item.description: Last gen with current gen performance. | It may be a 2025 model, but the AMD Ryzen AI 300 CPU in the Lenovo ThinkPad T14 Gen 6 AMD delivers the same performance as a more modern Ryzen AI 400 chip. With rising prices, it may be worth to buy the older Lenovo laptop, despite its successor already being announced.
